texts: four month opnsense diy router build wanted to finally report back on my extremely cursed optiplex opnsense build from a while ago huge thanks to uautian and rsleepingoptiplex for kicking this whole thing off specs dell optiplex 5055 sff upgraded to a 32mb bios chip running a padded biostar x470 bios ryzen 5700g 16gb ram intel x710t4l why i did this to myself i needed a new opnsense router after discovering that my old i78700 box simply could not keep up with 10gbps routing once wireguard and intervlan traffic were involved it technically worked but it was clearly suffering i also wanted the router off the rack so i could finally move the rack around the condo without rewiring half my life naturally this turned into a quick project that took four months the build from hell this whole thing started when i saw uautians sleeper optiplex build he figured out how to crossflash the bios on a 5055 sff to get around dells ridiculous firmware limits the tradeoff was brutal but tempting you lose the pcie x4 slot and basically all voltage control but you gain support for ryzen 5000 on what is effectively a first or second gen ryzen platform the pcie layout on the 5055 sff is terrible once the x4 slot is gone you are left with one nvme x4 slot and one pcie x16 slot that is only wired x8 that was it my original plan was two nics plus a gpu that plan died quickly we did discover the smbus tape trick which technically allows the x4 slot to function again for some devices i tried it with an extra nic but it was flaky and i did not trust it long term i also tried running an arc a310 out of the m2 slot using risers paired with a 5950x i went pretty deep on this including replacing the stock 16mb bios chip with a 32mb spi soic8 chip to discover any 32mb bioses that would give the x4 slot back there are only two chips that actually exist on the market and only one is close to dells original spec i tested every viable 32mb bios image i could find to no avail after months of waiting on parts risers and adapters i finally admitted defeat on the gpu idea i padded the most stable 16mb bios dropped in a 5700g and called it the nic drama the next problem was the network card i wanted a single nic that could do everything my modem is 25gbe but i wanted multiple 10gbe ports for lacp and general flexibility the x710t4l was perfect on paper the system refused to post with the card installed after way too much troubleshooting the smbus tape trick turned out to be the fix that at least made the system boot reliably with the card installed it also gave me some hope for the x4 slot but in my testing it was never stable enough to trust and absolutely did not work with gpus once opnsense was up and running and i had migrated my old config i ran into the next issue the x710 refused to negotiate 25 or 5 gig speeds only 1g or 10g it turned out the card was actually a dell x710t4lt dell had flashed it with oem firmware that deliberately disables multigig support i still do not understand why anyone would do this after several hours of digging i found this gist i adapted it for my setup reflashed the card and finally got proper 25g negotiation at that point the build was effectively done and i mounted it on the wall wiring mistakes were made since i was already deep in this project i decided to upgrade all the condo wiring and move to fiber where possible this was a mistake the building is only about five years old but whoever did the low voltage work decided that conduits were optional every cable was stapled in place after pulling the junction box and doing some boroscope exploration it became clear that none of the runs were pullable absolute nonsense i cut back any sections that might have been damaged and reterminated everything with cat6arated pullthrough keystones i did the same on the media closet side all runs were under about 20 meters and somehow every single one negotiated 10g with zero errors i got very lucky replacing the junction box with a hybrid old work and new work box was its own nightmare but i eventually got it aligned and secured final stretch once the wiring was done swapping in the new opnsense router should have been easy it almost was i will spare everyone my full rant about qnap lite managed switches but the short version is that the web ui cannot be assigned to a specific vlan twelve hours later after way too much trial and error everything was finally working when i powered off the old opnsense box the entire network came back up instantly no drama no weird issues everything just worked i think i earned that last bit of relief was it worth it the scope of this project spiraled way beyond what i expected and it took about four months from start to finish that said i ended up with a compact silent wallmounted 10gb opnsense router that does exactly what i want now i just have an extra 2u of space at the front of the rack staring at me related posts

atmosphere special issue the effect of heliogeomagnetic activity in the geoenvironment and by extension to human health and heliobiology summary linked issue summary recent scientific data in heliobiology often overlapping with chronobiology meteobiology and magnetobiology primarily consists of studies exploring correlations between space weather events solar flares geomagnetic storms and various biological effects particularly on human health the current scientific consensus acknowledges a growing body of evidence for these effects though the precise biological mechanisms remain a major area of ongoing research key recent findings 20242025 heightened solar activity the sun is currently in an active phase near or at its solar maximum of cycle 25 expected to peak around mid2025 which has led to a significant increase in space weather events including major geomagnetic storms in may and october 2024 this provides an unprecedented opportunity for data collection on biological impacts neurological and physiological effects recent medical studies continue to show correlations between heliogeomagnetic activity and neurologicalcardiological problems circadian rhythm and sleep researchers hypothesize that geomagnetic fluctuations may interfere with melatonin production and circadian rhythms leading to disrupted sleep patterns heightened fatigue and altered mood during periods of high solar activity brain activity studies have established that weak to moderate geomagnetic storms can reduce the brains convulsive threshold potential mechanisms the ongoing research is moving beyond just correlation to investigate potential physical mechanisms magnetite nanoparticles the presence of magnetite nanoparticles in the human brain is a leading theory suggesting these particles could influence specific organs and glands based on the timevarying geomagnetic field radical pairs and cryptochromes another proposed mechanism involves radical pairs and cryptochrome proteins which are already linked to magnetoreception in some animals and circadian rhythms in various organisms intracellular water changes in intracellular water structure forming exclusion zone water due to enhanced magnetic fields are also being explored as a potential mechanism for cellular activation summary of the field regarding heliobiology the scientific community is focusing efforts on understanding the howthe specific atomicmolecular mechanisms that explain how weak magnetic fields can influence complex biosystems

a touch of a story from a dream i had this morning i would appreciate it that if you read this and let me know your honest thoughts on the content like if you would read this book type thinking 2nd world liminial warrior as i wake i find myself resting in a concrete hallway outside of a busy travel area that it seems only i can reach i can feel that you are reading this and that a being is typing part of me into existence i have spent 5 days walking away from the busy travel area but never found a twist or turn or door or archway or anything but a concrete hallway it took 5 days to get back here so i took a nap el eieen char rand my constant companion this little wide eyed owl popped into my existence when i signed up at the liminals exploration guild i call her ein rand based off an author from earth ayn rand here in this liminal world it is often the second space for people here the ones lucky enough to survive and find a busy travel area or as you can see a bta in btas in liminial space they are a kind of stabilized nexus where the energy from the many different beings keep it connected to one another making it a constant and convenient meeting space of sorts if you ever find yourself trapped in a limitation space and find yourself safe try to feel for a bta you have to feel it inside you like a string you can grab with your mind that feels of many beings that way grab that feeling and once you phase into a bta try to find the liminals exploration guild they almost always have a person that can speak an earth language but thats only if you come from an earth that has felt the liminal space before if they dont speak your language then you just landed yourself a job at the guild my friend its almost like they collect languages at the guild so fear not and teach them all you know and they will pay you for every page you write i awoke from my nap because i felt that someone from an earth could see this existence i have so when they began writing about it i figured id help them out and explain and let myself be documented to explain this world as i see it on your earth if you find it has a following for liminial space type things that means you and your plane of existence are connected and you or anyone could end up here at anytime anywhere in any unexplored unexplainable area it could be haunted it could be peaceful it could be natural it could be artificial it could be anything so do not take the plane of liminial space lightly its far more dangerous than it is peaceful well if you do find yourself in this place quickly make sure you are safe you will always know when you arent because inside that liminial feeling there will be an ominous danger feeling mixed in if you can go back the way you came if you can go back that means you are stuck here you must use all your senses to survive stay low stay quiet and keep moving slowly and methodically chase the feeling of safety chase the feeling of beings grouped together i you are lucky you might get found by a decent guild member if youre not well then all you can do is try your best and try to find your way to a bta and then to the guild dont hope for it but who knows you might be found by me and ein rand sometime the sudden appearance of a being will set off an alarm type feeling in guild explorers like me you have around a 30 30 30 chance the first 30 is a dangerous liminal explorer the next 30 is a guild sanctioned liminial explorer the last thirty is youre either ignored or the explorers just havent felt your arrival and then theres this last bit of your chance its not good you could be off in what we think are closed areas or you could have arrived in a dangerous area where predatory things stalk i mean its not like liminial space is fully known most anything and everything seems to happen here so i wish you luck so far the guild has mapped over a trillion acres of general liminial space and several hundred billion acres of personal liminial space its not like anyone can go everywhere thats just not how liminial space works heres an example the areas around dense nexus entry points have all been heavily padded and softened because if you touch or are touched when phasing into an area there is a repelling force based on the beings density so lets say a normal 180 pound earth human phase touches a normal 90 pound earth human the 90 pounder is going to be repelled more than the 180 pounder its not likely that either one is going to be standing after a phase touch so there is that okay now general liminial areas and personal liminial areas they are as they sound a general liminial area is just that many people know and can use that area personal liminial areas are just that as well its either just one person can use the space or very few can and when i say use the space i mean it like they can use it to travel or make a home or a shortcut or get to a general liminial area then there are the rumored closed off spaces andor predatory stalking areas these always make any being with self preservation instincts feel on edge there are beings that are rumored to have been in a closed off liminial space and they dont understand how they got to or from the general area but its liminial space so unless the causation and closed off area get documented a lot then theres no way to really prove it its like a pickpocket if you cant catch them with their and in your pocket and they run you might never see them again its not like you can easily hunt down criminals in liminial space that pick pocket could have an enormous treasure room that no other being can enter and unless you actually see where they phase into their hoard you probably wont be getting anything back and wont be able prove anything after that so thats a very light run down of this liminial space that i seem to exist in at least to me it feels like i do and i believe in that feeling yatkicid had no idea what this meant when it popped up in the sung notes app but once i looked it up it fit so il leaving it like the ending to a journal entry

my experience as a brand new player greetings all im writing this with currently 333 hours recorded on steam i dont know if this will be of interest but i heard that the developers do browse the subreddit so if nothing else itll be some feedback for the team i had previously tried eve back in 2016 played for 2 days got overwhelmed and didnt touch it again until a week ago im older now and i suppose now rather than feeling frustrated at not being able to understand everything immediately i have no come to enjoy that feeling of everything being unknown and being able to immerse myself in learning various systems of new games that i try for me that feeling of learning is now fun and part of the excitement rather than frustrating and tedious this theme of maturity is also something that i appreciate about the game the ui and menus even the in game shop have an air of being grown up i knew eve came out 20 years ago and looked at some of the screenshots of the game in the past and i thought its really quite cool how the developers have iterated with the ui over the years and kept it feeling modern with just enough flash scifi flare so i logged in and decided to pick up where i left off over 9 years ago and continue with my essentially newborn character i had some plex left over which was enough for me to upgrade to an omega account since i thought i might as well use it than letting it collect dust in the vault and if i didnt get the game this time well chances are i wouldnt becoming back for a 3rd time anyway what struck me first was i presume a new way the skills were organised in the ui for new players i must have spent at least 15 minutes just clicking around the career program looking at what paths to get started with again it felt digestible and i didnt get a feeling of being totally overwhelmed with the amount of things to click on i had the mindset that i was just going to sit down and immerse myself in the game and see what happens i decided to take a look at exploration and realised i had completed the agent missions way back when so i figured well lets do some exploring whatever that entails the video explaining how to use probes to scan for cosmic things i cant remember what theyre called off the top of my head lol was really helpful and i took a couple of jumps out of my home system and started scanning and probing away i thought that since i was in a high security region of space that there wouldnt be much to explore and whatever loot i did find wouldnt be that great but again i just wanted to try and immerse myself and learn how things worked i start probing around and found a wormhole i purposefully didnt search anything up since i just wanted to enjoy discovering the game for myself i was honestly kind of hesitant to travel through it because after inspecting it for a moment it said that it was due to collapse within a specified number of hours well that could mean 5 minutes from now or 12 hours from now was i going to go through this thing and be completely trapped and on my own in a far flung region of the galaxy i thought so be it and bit the bullet and went through the solar system i ended up in had a few more wormholes but honestly i was too nervous to go another layer deep so i found a data site and thought to myself perfect time to go loot as i jumped to the site to my dismay i noticed about a dozed red triangles appear on my overview windows and proceeded to get annihilated by whatever hostiles were defending this site honestly it was freaking awesome lol feeling like i had naively walked into some guarded ancient tomb or something for which i was woefully unprepared i asked around and someone explained to me the different types of sites and risks associated with them so i knew for next time the next day i determinedly fumbled around and managed to find a site where i wasnt immediately destroyed and found some decenti guess i cant even remember what i found but it sold for a few 100k so i considered it a win loot i browsed the agency window for a bit and found planetary industry which i figured would be cool to try out and maybe i could generate some passive income i ended up setting up some oxygen extraction near a gas giant nearby again i didnt really care if what i was doing wasnt optimal i just wanted to throw myself into the eve experience so to speak after a while i came to the realisation that i had no idea where the hell i was i could open the map and see my location obviously but where did everyone hang out at this point i thought that i should probably get some help so submitted an application to eve university and the folk in the corporation channel were helpful in pointing me towards where their base was and it would probably be a good idea to set up somewhere close to there so i packed up and hauled my arse and my every possesion across the galaxy terrified i was going to lose everything to some pirate along the way i had made about 500k isk from selling my oxygen and took time on the voyage to explore the various menus of the game as someone who enjoys systems based games factorio europa universalis etc i found the entire design of the markets quite fascinating as well as clicking through tool tips to follow various paths a raw material may take on its way to become a multitude of finished products it hit me that this a true sandbox and i felt a sense of freedom that i hadnt got when trying out other mmos which have always felt a bit railroaded and therefore a bit bland to me insofar as they dont have the sort of emergent dynamic gameplay that eve could offer i think that potential is a big part of the reason i want to keep playing but at the same time i understand how difficult it is to really communicate that to potential new players im planning to attend a some classes with eve uni and hopefully learn some more gameplay mechanics and make some friends in game that was definitely one of the barriers to me playing previously i dont have any friends in real life that are interested in eve so i knew i would be tackling this alone overall im really excited to get stuck in i certainly see how this game appeals to a certain type of person and honestly i regret not giving it another go sooner yasha lexan

i built and shipped a mobile game using expo react native heres my workflow tools and early monetization learnings hi everyone i wanted to share a small project called wop im a product designer by background not a fulltime engineer so this was also an exercise in keeping the stack and workflow as simple as possible the project wop is a casual shortsession mobile game designed for quick play the goal wasnt depth or progressionheavy gameplay but something lightweight that can be opened played and closed in a couple of minutes tech stack app expo managed workflow react native typescript i deliberately went with expo to reduce friction around native setup and focus on shipping rather than infrastructure design very limited use of figma i only used it for highlevel visuals and basic layout exploration most ui decisions were made directly in code and adjusted iteratively on device backend services no heavy backend dependency game sessions are short and mostly local revenuecat for subscriptions and paywall experimentation workflow process 1 start in code not design tools as a product designer this was intentional for this type of app i found it faster to roughly define visuals build directly in react native adjust spacing motion and interaction on device 2 expo for speed hot reload expo go allowed very fast iteration without constantly rebuilding native binaries 3 ship early i already had a previous app built with capacitor so this time i wanted to reduce complexity ship faster learn from real usage instead of polishing endlessly distribution growth published on ios and android created tiktok and instagram accounts to test lightweight organic distribution no paid acquisition so far current state 500 users 0 subscriptions at the moment monetization learnings so far freemium is harder than it looks getting installs is much easier than convincing users to pay im currently iterating on paywall visibility value communication when and how the paywall is triggered this is still very early but its been a good reality check why im sharing im mainly interested in feedback around whether expo rn is the right choice longterm for this kind of game monetization patterns that actually work for small casual games anything in the workflow that looks inefficient or naive if this isnt a good fit for the sub feel free to remove it if anyone wants to try it to better understand the feedback android ios happy to answer questions and share more details if useful

cannons shouldnt be the core damage for ship combat but should instead strip armour from sea creatures after going through the sailing opinion poll there was one idea that i had which i felt warranted a bit more elaboration because i genuinely think it would give the most design space for interesting ship combat i like cannons conceptually but the problem with them is that theyre slow and make ship combat essentially feel like a minigame disconnected entirely from one of the most core systems in the game to me the solution isnt to buff them into oblivion nor is it to just make regular attacks from your boat the best approach but to do a little bit of both if sea creatures had flat armour that made regular attacks ineffective until it was stripped with cannon fire that would help balance both aspects and keep ship combat feeling unique without feeling isolated from the rest of the game for example you engage an enemy with a few shots from a cannon to strip away the armour then kill it with a hail of arrows or magic theres so much that could be done using a hybrid and in my eyes it would fix both core issues in one fell swoop cannonballs wouldnt be needed in the insane numbers that they currently are but wouldnt be completely unnecessary ship combat would no longer feel entirely isolated from the rest of the combat system but it would feel distinct from regular combat i think theres a ton of design space that could be explored with this too you could fire a grapple instead of a cannonball to drag an enemy aboard your ship for melee combat you could have a humanoid enemy that boards your ship and attacks you directly you could have enemy ships that require exclusively cannonballs for direct boat damage or ships that need to be boarded and the crew killed with regular combat it also helps balance the different sailing enemies with respect to regular combat progression early enemies wont have much flat armour so if youre already incredibly powerful then you can just attack them directly and essentially overpower that armour however once you get to high level kraken or sharks you need to actually engage them using the ship before your regular attacks it also means that regular combat skills become necessary for later sailing enemies since even if you strip the armour youll still hit like a wet noodle unless your combat is up to snuff

plain text to html without losing formatting developers work with the plain text format almost everywhere from api responses to logs and user input fields storing and processing plain text is simple however this format doesnt carry much layout or structure this introduces a problem when plain text needs to appear in an html page users expect line breaks to stay in place and spacing to remain readable but browsers treat raw text very differently for example a user copies some paragraphs and log data from a text editor like notepad into a browserbased editor the paragraphs could merge together since html doesnt treat line breaks as structure and log data might collapse into one long line these issues are everywhere as you might have experienced firsthand before they commonly appear in contentrich platforms like documentation tools and project management systems hence its crucial that your text editor preserves plain text even after your users paste it this article explores why formatting breaks during conversion how html interprets plain text and which techniques you can use to protect structure key takeaways plain text format is simple and universal but it lacks structure making html conversion challenging browsers collapse whitespace by default causing plain text spacing and alignment to break html requires structural elements like ltpgt ltbrgt and ltpregt to preserve readable formatting manual parsing gives full control over how plain text becomes html but requires more development effort wysiwyg editors automate most basic conversion tasks by detecting structure during paste reducing manual work understanding the plain text format plain text offers a simple and transparent way to store content this is because it contains only characters and doesnt include metadata about fonts styling or layout this simplicity helps developers and end users process it with many tools but it also creates challenges during html conversion what plain text format can and cant represent the plain text format stores letters numbers symbols spaces tabs and line breaks these characters appear exactly as written because plain text doesnt support styling or layout as there are no rules for headings or alignment a plain text file contains only the characters the author typed plain text may use either ascii or unicode ascii covers basic english characters while unicode supports many writing systems emojis and symbols unicode matters during conversion because browsers must interpret each code point correctly when it comes to spacing plain text is literal for instance if the file shows four spaces it contains four space characters html will not preserve those characters unless developers enforce whitespace rules press enter or click to view image in full size alignleft note ascii or the american standard code for information interchange is a character encoding standard that assigns unique numbers 0127 to english letters digits punctuation and control codes tab new line in short its responsible for converting text into numbers that computers can understand eg a is 65 and a is 97 note on the other hand unicode is a character encoding standard that builds upon what the ascii already provides like ascii it assigns a unique number to every character however it can accommodate emojis and other languages and scripts this is because unicode has a potential code space of over a million character identifiers code points unicode uses different encoding forms including the popular utf8 why formatting breaks during html conversion preserving plain text format isnt part of htmls responsibilities it does have some remedies for this as youll see later its rendering rules come from early web standards that prioritized semantic structure over visual fidelity because of this browsers must interpret whitespace line breaks and special characters according to htmls layout model as a result browsers collapse whitespace by default several spaces shrink into one visible space and tabs collapse or convert into a small number of spaces this behavior breaks alignment for logs or structured text line breaks that use characters like n fail to create new paragraphs instead you must convert these into ltbrgttags or wrap sections in block elements you need to escape characters like lt and to avoid broken markup or injection vulnerability issues this is because they have special meaning in html what html expects html expects content inside elements that define structure for example paragraphs need a ltpgt tag line breaks need ltbrgttags and code belongs in ltpregt or ltcodegt blocks browsers dont infer these elements from plain text alone since htmls rendering engine collapses whitespace by design as stated earlier whitespace needs explicit rules you can use ltpregt tags or css rules like whitespace pre to override this behavior and preserve the literal spacing you must decide which parts of the input should keep exact alignment because preserving everything can cause unintended spacing hidden characters or inconsistent indentation how html interprets the plain text format html follows rendering rules that control spacing flow and structure it ignores consecutive spaces unless the text appears inside special elements or styles this behavior works for narrative text but may break content that relies on alignment html relies on structure and blocklevel elements shape how text appears for example a paragraph tag enforces vertical spacing while a ltdivgt creates a container with its own rules without these structures the browser treats the plain text format input as one continuous block furthermore line breaks appear only when you use tags like ltbrgt or when you preserve it using ltpregt tags tabs may also behave inconsistently between browsers with some treating them as a single space and some as consecutive spaces because of these inconsistencies alignments and spacing could break common developer techniques for converting plain text to html thankfully there are many ways to reliably convert plain text format to html no single method works for every scenario so choose based on your content type and project needs you can even combine them together for a more layered approach manual conversion using custom logic custom logic starts with treating the plain text as a stream of characters rather than a block of content with this youll typically read the text line by line and then decide how each line maps to html for example blank lines can turn into paragraph breaks while lines that start with a hyphen turn into list items these rules follow a structured logic detecting patterns assigning meaning and wrapping with the correct html custom logic is also versatile as it works for your specific use case if your end users write documentation for example you can interpret as a list when converting to plain text format escaping should happen first so the parser never confuses user text with actual html this includes replacing lt or gt and elements with html entities before applying any structural rules once the text is safe the script can assign the appropriate html tags to build the final converted content this approach works when you need full control over how users text becomes html it also helps generate predictable output that matches the exact needs of your project the tradeoff is that you must define the entire structure and conversion logic in code using builtin or languagelevel utilities many languages include small helper functions that solve the most basic parts of conversion for example phps nl2br turns newline characters n or rn into html line break tags ltbrgt similarly htmlspecialchars escapes characters that can alter markup eg lt gt this function is also crucial since it helps prevent crosssite scripting xss which involves injecting scripts that can execute in client browsers for example with htmlspecialchars you can turn scripts like ltscriptgtalertxssltscriptgt into harmless text ltscriptgtalertxssltscriptgt this is necessary for when youre displaying any userprovided or external data especially within form fields press enter or click to view image in full size alignleft while incredibly useful and essential these utilities cant handle more advanced formatting for example multispace indentation can collapse unless you add custom logic tabs also need normalization to avoid alignment issues using ltpregt and cssbased preservation some content needs exact alignment rather than semantic structure and logs stack traces and configuration files fall into this category wrapping them in ltpregt tags instructs the browser to respect every space tab and newline css rules such as whitespace prewrap preserve this behavior and allow lines to wrap inside narrow layouts while this approach keeps the visual pattern of the source it doesnt express relationships in html form for instance a block of text inside ltpregt has no paragraphs lists or headings thus it works best when readability depends on fixed spacing rather than document structure plain text formatmarkdownhtml conversion interestingly some plain text already resembles markdown when you list down items in text editors the natural way is to use dashes right this is the same in markdown and many users naturally format plain text following markdown conventions without realizing it instead of writing custom logic to detect ordered lists or other formatting you can map common patterns to markdown tokens afterwards you can pass the result through a markdown parser to generate html cleanly these parsers can also handle mixed input as they simply interpret what they can and ignore what they cant this method does come with some weaknesses first input that doesnt resemble markdown at all wont benefit from this approach eg a log file some users may also type symbols that resemble markdown unintentionally which can lead to unexpected formatting using external libraries most ecosystems provide libraries that convert plain text into structured html these tools often include configurable rules for paragraphs indentations lists and block detection some allow developers to attach preprocessors so that you can handle unusual patterns without modifying the core library these libraries could also cover edge cases that appear in realworld text like inconsistent spacing or mixed encodings using wysiwyg editors a wysiwyg html editor provides another easy way to handle converting plain text format to html modern editors may apply conversion rules when users paste text preserving line breaks and clear structural cues they may also come with paste handlers which detect list markers indentation or repeated whitespace what makes this method simpler is that youll get plain text to html support from the start the editor handles the heavy lifting by analyzing pasted content and transforming it into structured elements like paragraphs line breaks nonbreaking spaces etc alignleft its important to note that like the other methods wysiwyg editors dont present an absolute solution to everything you might still have to rely on other means for automatically detecting markdown code and other advanced formatting still with these tools you skip most of the work like creating a custom plain text format to html converter note click here to see how you can get started with a wysiwyg editor implementation of plain text to html conversion conclusion converting plain text format into html requires careful handling of whitespace encoding structure and escaping each technique supports different goals and its up to you to choose whats best for your use case manual parsing offers full control css rules preserve visual alignment and libraries and wysiwyg editors reduce complexity browsers and editors follow rules that shape how plain text appears so understanding these rules can help you build stable and predictable conversion workflows in the end the best approach depends on your content logs documentation etc its structure and your users needs the article was originally published on the froala blog

how carving forks support better control and safer cutting in the kitchen kitchen tools often work best when they are used together while knives are essential for cutting they depend on supporting utensils to function safely and accurately one such tool is the carving fork often described as a fork for meat this utensil is designed to provide stability and control during slicing tasks though it may appear simple its role in food preparation is practical and well defined this article explores carving forks in detail focusing on how they are used why they matter and how they contribute to safer and more consistent results in everyday cooking the goal is to provide clear useful information that helps home cooks understand when and why a carving fork is worth using what a carving fork is designed to do a carving fork is a long handled utensil with pointed prongs that are intended to hold food in place while it is being cut most carving forks feature two prongs though some designs include three for added grip unlike dining forks carving forks are built for strength and reach rather than comfort at the table the primary purpose of a carving fork is to secure large cuts of food particularly meat during slicing by anchoring the food to the cutting surface the fork allows the knife to move smoothly and evenly this combination improves accuracy and reduces unnecessary movement why carving forks are useful in everyday cooking stability during cutting large cuts of meat can be difficult to manage especially when they are freshly cooked and still warm a carving fork holds the meat firmly in place preventing it from sliding across the cutting board this added stability helps produce cleaner slices and reduces interruptions during carving safer hand positioning using a fork for meat instead of fingers keeps hands away from the knife blade this is especially important when applying pressure to dense or uneven foods the carving fork acts as a buffer between the user and the cutting edge supporting safer technique better portion control consistent slices are easier to achieve when the food is stable a meat carving fork helps guide the knife making it easier to cut even portions this can be useful for both presentation and serving common situations where carving forks are used carving forks are often associated with large meals but their usefulness extends beyond special occasions they are commonly used for slicing roasted chicken or turkey carving beef pork or lamb roasts handling slow cooked meats such as brisket turning or lifting large cuts during preparation managing hot food directly from the oven or grill in some kitchens carving forks are also used when cutting large vegetables that require extra control such as squash or melon key design features of carving forks prong length and shape the prongs of a carving fork are longer and thicker than those of a standard fork this allows them to penetrate deeply into meat without bending sharp tips help the fork grip the food securely while proper spacing between the prongs improves balance two prongs are common because they allow for precise placement and easier removal after slicing handle construction the handle of a carving fork is typically extended to keep hands farther from heat and blades a comfortable handle shape supports a secure grip and reduces strain during use handles may be straight or slightly contoured depending on the design the focus is on control rather than decoration balance and weight a carving fork should feel stable in the hand proper balance ensures that the fork responds predictably to movement which is important when holding food steady excessively heavy or poorly balanced forks can make carving more difficult materials used in carving forks stainless steel prongs stainless steel is commonly used for carving fork prongs due to its strength and resistance to rust it maintains its shape under pressure and is easy to clean stainless steel also supports sharp tips that remain effective over time with proper care wooden and bamboo handles wood and bamboo handles are often chosen for their natural feel and comfortable grip bamboo is lightweight and durable when treated correctly these materials also stay cooler to the touch compared to metal handles synthetic handle materials some carving forks feature handles made from composite or resin materials these are designed to resist moisture and cracking making them suitable for frequent use the relationship between carving forks and knives a carving fork works best when paired with a suitable carving knife while the knife performs the cutting the fork provides resistance and control together they create a balanced system that supports accurate slicing matching the length and weight of the fork to the knife can improve overall handling when both tools feel comfortable carving requires less effort and produces better results using a carving fork effectively securing the meat to use a carving fork properly insert the prongs into the thickest part of the meat apply steady pressure to hold it in place but avoid forcing the fork too deeply the goal is stability not compression coordinating with the knife position the fork so it counteracts the motion of the knife slight angling can help prevent the meat from shifting this coordination allows the knife to slice cleanly through the food turning and lifting food carving forks can also be used to lift or rotate large cuts of meat when doing so ensure the prongs are fully inserted to avoid slipping this is especially helpful when repositioning food during carving cleaning and maintaining carving forks washing after use carving forks should be cleaned soon after use to prevent residue from drying on the prongs hand washing is often recommended particularly for forks with wooden or bamboo handles drying and storage thorough drying helps prevent moisture damage carving forks can be stored in utensil drawers holders or on magnetic boards provided the prongs are protected long term care although carving fork prongs do not require frequent sharpening keeping them clean and free from corrosion helps maintain performance avoid using carving forks for tasks that could bend or damage the prongs carving forks in modern home kitchens despite changes in cooking trends carving forks remain relevant because they address a specific need large cuts of food still require stability and knives alone cannot always provide it carving forks continue to support careful preparation and thoughtful technique in kitchens that emphasize efficiency and safety carving forks contribute to a smoother workflow they are not limited to formal meals and can be used whenever control is needed during cutting choosing a carving fork for your kitchen selecting a carving fork depends on how often it will be used and what types of food are typically prepared a sturdy meat carving fork may be useful for frequent roasting while occasional use may call for a simpler design comfort balance and material quality are important factors to consider a fork that feels natural in the hand is more likely to be used correctly and consistently final thoughts carving forks are practical tools that support safer and more controlled food preparation by holding food steady and keeping hands at a safe distance from the blade they improve both efficiency and confidence in the kitchen understanding how carving forks work how they are designed and when to use them allows home cooks to make better use of their kitchen tools whether preparing a large roast or managing everyday meals a reliable fork for meat plays an important role in achieving clean consistent results

willingness to sit with discomfort without judgment has helped a lot of people especially men finally feel seen instead of pathologized his integration of psychiatry neuroscience and eastern thoughts on designing a good life about a year ago i wrote a post here titled from the other side what happens after fi which sparked more thoughtful discussion than i expected as we wind down 2025 i wanted to share a few reflections on something adjacent but broader specifically how ive been thinking about designing a good life we all start from different places financially and otherwise but one thing ive increasingly come to believe is that a good life doesnt happen automatically even after fi instead it takes intention as with my previous posts im sharing because writing these things down helps me consolidate my own thoughts and because it might be useful to others as well 1 in the abstract most people tend to share quite a bit in common when it comes to what they believe makes a good life there is a huge body of work around this much ink time and effort has been spent by people trying to understand what makes a good life the harvard happiness study countless wellbeing theories and academic papers even notable personal finance folks like ben felix writing about it at a high level i find that the findings converge surprisingly well most of us seem to want meaning or purpose often through work or contribution strong relationships and connection a sense of competence or mastery over something good physical and mental health enough positive emotion and vitality to enjoy our days there are numerous frameworks that try to encapsulate these ideas eg permav llllife but they all largely point to pretty similar desires 2 but how you achieve it is deeply personal while the destination may be similar the paths are not we all have different temperaments talents interests and energy levels what feels deeply engaging to one person may feel mindnumbingly boring to another trying to copy someone elses life especially someone who is just wired differently from you rarely works ive found this to be one of the subtler traps postfi benchmarking lifestyles instead of designing one that actually fits you ultimately many of these decisions involve tradeoffs that only you can make for example how much personal space do you want versus the need to connect with loved ones how much does social status matter to you versus your willingness to conform to societal expectations how do you balance personal ambition with the sacrifices required there are no right answers only an answer that is right for you 3 exploration usually beats introspection the question then usually becomes how do you find what actually fits you my sense is i dont think the right life is something you figure out purely by thinking harder more often its something you discover through trying things small experiments matter new routines hobbies ways of working ways of interacting with people do you prefer going to big social events or having small group chats do you enjoy teaching what do you like to learn most wont stick and thats fine the information you get from trying is far more valuable than what you get from just thinking in your head about what might work to be clear im not saying introspection doesnt matter reflecting on your experiences is important but it needs input ive found it hard to think my way into an ideal life that fits without living a few versions of it first 4 for things that matter rely on systems not motivation once you find things that genuinely matter to you build systems around them i used to unconsciously go weeks on occasion even months without seeing my parents even though we all live in singapore and have a good relationship i also struggled to consistently exercise meditate read or make space for hobbies despite really wanting to about a year ago i wrote down what mattered to me and turned most of it into recurring calendar events to myself among other things i now have recurring slots for date night visiting my parents nature walks meditation strength training catchups with close friends and family financial planning learning music this sounds rigid to some people but ive found it oddly liberating it removes the need to constantly renegotiate priorities with myself and frees up mental energy for things that genuinely require more conscious thought 5 leave room for slack serendipity and an unhurried pace that said life is unpredictable and not everything can or needs to be planned in advance i deliberately schedule more time than necessary to get places between meetings and when travelling it gives me more time to smell the flowers along the way and provides a buffer in case something unexpected happens we dont try to see every attraction on holiday if theres really a lot we want to do or see we try to stay longer if not we move on the goal isnt optimization its pleasure enjoyment and ease an unhurried life creates space for unexpected conversations ideas and moments ive come to value that more than squeezing every drop out of a schedule 6 use money deliberately in service of what matters i tend to be skeptical of blanket advice like spend on experiences not things or die with zero money is just a tool the right question isnt what category youre spending on but what it enables and what youre trading off some examples from my own life a home weights set made it much more convenient to work out which helped me get stronger lose weight and feel better about my body redesigning our living space made it more inclusive enabling many more meaningful conversations with friends and family buying my aunt a highquality sofa something shed never buy for herself has brought me outsized joy every time i see her delight in using it hosting gatherings at our place a few times a year is costly but helps us preserve relationships with people we care about some of these were things others experiences the common thread is that they directly supported things that matter to me and what i say i care about one of the systems my wife and i use to manage our finances is expense tracking but the goal isnt just affordability or making sure we dont run out of money thats of course important but its equally about ensuring were using money deliberately to advance our wellbeing and life aspirations 7 freedom is still the most important thing money can buy the older i get the more this feels true the biggest flex isnt a big house a fancy car or expensive holidays its the freedom to spend time with people you care about the freedom to work on things that interest you and just as importantly the freedom to leave toxic jobs unhealthy dynamics bad situations as ive mentioned before this isnt binary there are degrees of freedom and money helps unlock them in increasing measures 8 the best returns in life come from compounding someone once said all benefits in life come from compound interest whether in money relationships love health activities or habits im not sure i believe it fully but compounding has certainly produced some rich fruits in my life so far my best relationships are those that have lasted decades my favourite hobby is one ive been doing for over 25 years my marriage today works better than it did when we first got together i am way better at my professional job and i enjoy it way more than i did 15 years ago once youve found something you like doing or a relationship you want to keep nurturing make a note of it and find ways to keep growing it over time while this is a personal finance forum ive always felt that money should ultimately be in service of a better life to address the elephant in the room designing your life is undeniably easier when you have a little more money that said having money doesnt necessarily translate into a good life in fact there are many examples of the exact opposite happening objectively rich people who are just miserable with their lives as always hope this has been helpful what do you think happy to chat more in the comments below

9 ways to prevent spreading and catching classroom germs as new research finds workplace absences are at a 15year high we reveal the top ways to stay safe at school workplace absences due to sickness are a growing problem in the uk and have reached a 15year high according to the chartered institute of personnel and development cipd as educators are the third mostaffected sector for missing work because of illness how can teaching assistants avoid catching and help prevent the spread of classroom germs using the latest guidance from the uk health security agency ukhsa we explore nine tips for helping to prevent and control but not eradicate illness and infections 1 hand hygiene children and young people should be taught why hand hygiene is so important for reducing the spread of germs every setting should ensure that access to liquid soap warm water and paper towels is available the guidance also states that bar soap should not be used alcohol hand sanitiser can be used if hands are not visibly dirty however it isnt effective against gastroenteritis such as norovirus hand washing for at least 20 seconds should be done by everyone after using the toilet before eating or handling food after playtime after touching animals also any cuts or skin abrasions should be covered with a waterproof dressing 2 respiratory and cough hygiene all educators know that coughs and sneezes spread diseases teaching pupils to cover their nose and mouth when doing so can reduce the spread of infections the guidance highlights the importance of teaching respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette such as covering your nose and mouth when coughing or sneezing disposing of used tissues in a waste bin washing your hands with soap and water before touching your eyes mouth and nose if no tissues are available coughing or sneezing into your inner elbow cleaning objects and surfaces contaminated with respiratory secretions pupils should be discouraged from spitting and sharing food or drinks too 3 cleaning cleaning isnt in a teaching assistants job description but there are certain things educators may want to do to help prevent illness from spreading settings should be clean to reduce the risk of illnesses detergent and water are recommended to remove most germs that lead to infection commonly touched surfaces should be cleaned frequently as well as areas that have contact with food or bodily fluids any member of staff involved with cleaning should be trained and have access to personal protective equipment ppe such as household gloves and aprons 4 toileting intimate care and sanitation all toilets should have access to their own toilet paper to avoid crosscontamination when in use everyone should have access to a sink with warm running water and liquid not bar soap preferably wallmounted paper towel dispensers should be next to the sinks with a footoperated wastepaper bin for teaching assistants who may change nappies or provide intimate care a designated changing space should be identified that is away from play facilities and fooddrink preparation or consumption areas have hand washing facilities staff should ensure they dispose of nappies by wrapping them in a plastic bag if appropriate clean childrens skin with a disposable wipe not flannels label nappy creams and lotions do not share with others wipe changing mats with soapy water or a mild detergent after each use and at the end of each day check mats weekly for tears and discard if the cover is damaged wash and dry their hands after every nappy change before handling another child and before leaving the room 5 ventilation letting fresh air into indoor spaces can remove stale air and help to dilute air that contains viral particles it also reduces the spread of respiratory infections to prevent the spread of illness keep occupied spaces well ventilated by opening windows and doors to let fresh air in 6 blood and bodily fluid encountering blood faeces saliva vomit or nasal discharges may be more common if youre a teaching assistant with first aid responsibilities however it could also impact you in the classroom the cleaning of any bodily fluids should be done immediately while wearing ppe such as gloves and an apron disposable paper towels or clothes should be used for cleaning blood and bodily fluids they should be disposed of immediately after use affected surfaces should be cleaned with a detergent and disinfectant that is effective against both bacteria and viruses 7 teach pupils about germs laced throughout the six tips above from the ukhsas guidance is the need to educate pupils about how illness spreads and the importance of hygiene the beginning of term is a great time to embed routines so before winter illnesses begin to spread establish expectations for hand washing and beyond 8 stay away from school if youre contagious workplace absences due to illness may be at a 15year high but its important that both staff and pupils stay at home if they are ill to prevent it spreading further ukhsa and nhs produced a guide on when to stay at home and for how long for diarrhoea and vomiting everyone should remain at home until 48 hours after their last episode however youre ok to go to school with tonsillitis if you feel well enough to do so read should i keep my child off school 9 tips from fellow educators as teaching assistants youll likely find yourself in close contact with illness throughout the school year and catching some of them will be inevitable you may take all of the above precautions but still get ill so fellow teaching assistants also recommend if youre eligible and want to getting the flu vaccine taking a daily multivitamin carrying hand sanitiser with you and using it frequently listening to your body and staying at home if youre unwell

what would be the most ideal itinerary for a weeklong trip to rann utsav in kutch every winter the white desert of kutch transforms into one of indias most unique cultural destinations with rann utsav in full swing thousands of travellers are heading to gujarat to experience the moonlit salt desert kutchi culture handicrafts and music most visitors arrive and depart via bhuj making it the perfect base to explore kutch at a relaxed pace if you are planning a rann utsav trip and wondering how to structure your days this 7day itinerary keeps things simple balanced and wellpaced you can easily shorten this to 5 days by skipping or merging a couple of days day 1 arrive in bhuj and explore heritage why this day matters bhuj is not just a transit point it is the cultural heart of kutch and a great introduction to the regions history and architecture places to cover aina mahal an 18thcentury palace known for its mirror work chandeliers and indoeuropean design prag mahal a grand italian gothic palace offering panoramic views of bhuj from its clock tower hamirsar lake a peaceful spot in the city centre ideal for an evening walk bhuj local markets great for kutchi embroidery bandhani textiles and silver jewellery stay bhuj travel bhuj airport or railway station connects well with major cities day 2 bhujodi craft village and drive to dhordo why this day matters this day connects kutchs living craft traditions with the rann utsav experience morning bhujodi village 8 km from bhuj famous for handloom weaving and traditional kutchi textiles you can see artisans at work and buy directly from them afternoon drive from bhuj to dhordo approx 80 km 2 to 25 hours check in at rann utsav tent city or nearby accommodations evening orientation walk inside tent city enjoy local food and folk performances stay dhordo rann utsav tent city day 3 white rann and rann utsav experience why this day matters this is the highlight of the trip and should be unhurried daytime leisure time at tent city optional activities like camel rides atv rides or craft stalls evening white rann sunset visit the vast salt desert turns golden and pink as the sun sets cultural night at rann utsav traditional kutchi music dance and performances night moonlit white desert on full moon nights the rann glows under moonlight and feels almost surreal stay dhordo day 4 kalo dungar and border landscapes why this day matters this day shows the dramatic geography of kutch beyond the salt desert places to cover kalo dungar black hill the highest point in kutch with sweeping views of the rann india bridge a symbolic location near the indopak border area entry subject to permissions hodka village known for mud houses embroidery and communitybased tourism evening return to dhordo or drive back toward bhuj depending on energy levels stay dhordo or bhuj day 5 craft villages of nirona and return to bhuj why this day matters this is where you see crafts that exist nowhere else in the world places to cover nirona village known for rogan art fabric painting using castor oil copper bell making lacquer wood craft interact with artisans and learn about the process behind their craft evening drive back to bhuj relaxed evening caf hopping or local shopping stay bhuj day 6 mandvi coastal day trip why this day matters this day offers a complete change of landscape from desert to sea places to cover mandvi beach clean calm and ideal for a relaxed morning vijay vilas palace a former royal palace known for its rajput architecture and film shoots windmill beach a unique sight where the coastline meets renewable energy infrastructure travel bhuj to mandvi approx 60 km 15 hours stay bhuj day 7 smritivan earthquake memorial and departure why this day matters ending the journey here adds depth and reflection to the trip smritivan earthquake memorial museum built on bhujiyo dungar smritivan is a 470acre memorial dedicated to the lives lost in the 2001 gujarat earthquake what makes it special seven immersive museum galleries the worlds largest miyawaki forest powerful storytelling through design and landscape panoramic sunrise and sunset viewpoints over bhuj it is a calm meaningful space that offers perspective and closure before leaving kutch departure bhuj airport or railway station ideal to schedule flights or trains in the afternoon or evening can this be done in 5 days yes if you are short on time combine day 4 and day 5 skip mandvi day 6 keep smritivan on the final day best time to visit november to february full moon dates enhance the white rann experience pleasant weather for sightseeing and travel final thoughts a rann utsav trip is not just about the white desert kutch is a region of stories crafts resilience and landscapes that change every day by starting and ending in bhuj and placing smritivan at the end this itinerary ensures your journey moves from celebration to reflection from spectacle to meaning if you are planning to visit rann utsav this season take a moment to slow down and explore kutch beyond the tents it is worth it

why inviteonly events outperform conferences why inviteonly events outperform conferences if you are a founder who has attended major conferences and gone home with lanyards only to feel a weird sense of not being affected you are one of many in the same position many enthusiastic entrepreneurs are very much on their own they feel pressured to scale and are always overloaded with information this disappointment is exactly what makes inviteonly events the number one choice for serious founders looking for clarity rather than noise the right setting could alter decisions sharpen the strategy and help the company reach its full potential where flight club mastermind can take on a leading role in driving positive change by providing founders with a highly valuable highly private event apply for inviteonly access why do large conferences often miss the mark for founders at first glance conferences are perfect a large number of people are attending an event impressive speakers busy agenda however many entrepreneurs would claim that this is far from being true the majority of conferences are suitable for many but shallow for individuals the advice given is simply good for everyone the networking moments are pushed to the very last minute during the break and it feels like everyone is fighting for attention to sell what they have with no one actually there to listen you might get to know several people at once but by the end of the event zero relationships had formed and none of them actually made an impact on your company the latest survey of founders found that more than 70 of respondents use the phrase inspired but unclear to describe their feelings suggesting they are motivated but unsure how to proceed the gap between attraction and accomplishment is exactly where growth surreptitiously stops one of the key reasons founders now prefer inviteonly events over large conferences apply to join the founders why are smaller curated experiences more attractive to founders as the company expands the consequences of its decisions gradually grow heavier changes in pricing employment of toplevel managers expansion into new markets such a small exclusive group of people changes the whole scenario the talks become more intense body language and sector terms carry the day one of the prerequisites for joining the group is demonstrating experience which helps build trust quickly within the framework of private groups founders are free to discuss openly cash flow troubles errors made in leadership deviations from growth trajectories subjects that are less likely to be brought up on conference stages a b2b saas founder who was a member of a closed mastermind said that the major change he had made was reducing his product roadmap from 14 features to just 5 such targeting alone enabled his team to deliver quickly and increased the conversiontocustomer percentage by almost 40 in just one quarter why inviteonly events help founders make faster decisions in inviteonly groups founders do not talk to share ideas they talk to make real decisions everyone in the room is actively building and growing a business so conversations quickly turn into action founders ask clear questions get honest answers and decide what to do next with more confidence speed matters at this stage waiting too long to decide often causes more damage than making a small mistake in small curated groups founders learn from others who have already faced similar problems this saves time and avoids repeated mistakes instead of leaving with long notes founders leave with a clear next step and a reason to act now how do inviteonly events create better conversations what makes private groups special is not their secrecy but their alignment everyone is noted for almost the same level of expertise drive and duty inviteonly events eliminate the stage of presentation and ego in these rooms the startup founders cease to be concerned with vanity metrics and switch their focus to actual limitations such as churn burn rate leadership fatigue decision paralysis in this context the counsel is not just the wisdom of experience it is also the learning from the trial of different approaches flight club mastermind is a very significant event in this whole picture especially for organizing the user experience network expansion and inperson time how inviteonly communities help founders feel less alone as a business grows founders often feel more isolated teams depend on them for direction investors expect certainty and friends outside the business may no longer understand the pressure inviteonly events foster a trusted space where founders can speak honestly in these groups discussions go beyond numbers and targets founders discuss leadership stress decisionmaking pressure and the emotional side of growth knowing that others face the same challenges brings relief and confidence this sense of connection is one of the biggest benefits of inviteonly events and explains why founders keep returning to these closeknit communities why does strategy become clearer in private masterminds scaling rarely improves when founders add more strategies it improves when they remove distractions when founders join a wellstructured mastermind they gain the space to think clearly and make better decisions allowing them to step back and view the business from a broad perspective the strategy sessions are becoming conversations rather than presentations a saas founder who had been stuck at 3 million in arr for 2 years explore flight club mastermind

traffic for years this is particularly powerful for planners templates and lifestyle products where visual appeal matters youtube is similar video content ranks on both youtube and google and tutorial videos that provide genuine value can drive traffic to your products for years after you publish them one well optimized video can bring you customers for the next decade without you doing anything else then email marketing is the backbone of it all you build a list by offering free resources that are genuinely valuable not garbage you threw together in an hour with chatgpt but stuff you could actually charge for then you nurture that list with helpful content stories and insights when you launch a product you have a warm audience that actually wants to hear from you and is primed to buy this is longterm strategy it takes six to twelve months to see serious results from content marketing and seo but these are the channels that drive sustainable income that grows every month not one off sales that you have to chase down individually they launch strategically not randomly when successful creators launch a product its not a casual hey i made a thing post they build anticipation for weeks through teaser content and waitlists they pre sell to their email list before the public launch so they make money before theyve even officially released it they collect testimonials from beta users who got early access in exchange for feedback they create urgency with limitedtime launch pricing or early bird bonuses they provide special bonuses for people who buy in the first 24 hours they follow up with abandoned cart sequences for people who showed interest but didnt buy they orchestrate a strategic launch campaign that might include multiple email sequences timed to land at optimal moments a social media content calendar that builds momentum webinars or live workshops that provide value while naturally leading to the product affiliate partnerships with other creators who have complementary audiences and only after all of that is working do they even consider paid advertising they dont just post a link and hope for the best they treat the launch like the major business event it is why just post and hope doesnt work anymore the digital product landscape has changed dramatically in 2016 you might have been able to throw a basic product on etsy with decent photos and make sales with minimal effort because the market was less saturated in 2026 not a chance sorry market saturation means there are millions of digital products competing for attention and most of them look the same platform algorithm changes on etsy amazon and other marketplaces mean they prioritize established sellers who have track records of sales and good reviews so new sellers struggle to get any visibility at all consumer sophistication has increased too buyers are smarter than ever more skeptical of low effort products and they can spot a cash grab from a mile away trust is everything now because people have been burned too many times by products that overpromised and underdelivered and quality expectations are astronomically higher than they used to be a basic pdf template that would have sold well five years ago wont cut it anymore when people expect beautiful design comprehensive content and ongoing support the digital product creators making real money in 2026 are going to be the ones who understand theyre not just selling a product theyre building a brand an audience and a reputation the product is almost secondary to the relationship and trust theyve built the reality check you need to hear i need to be honest with you about something most make money with digital products gurus wont tell you because theyre trying to sell you their course this is hard work building a profitable digital product business requires market research skills content creation abilities across multiple formats marketing knowledge that goes way beyond post on social media email marketing expertise including segmentation and automating workflows seo understanding so people can actually find you copywriting skills to persuade people to buy from you customer service capabilities because youll have questions and problems to handle and financial management because youre running an actual business with expenses and taxes and all that fun stuff its not really passive income like people hope it is thats a lie that gets repeated because it sounds appealing but its fundamentally dishonest sure once youve built your systems you can make sales while you sleep but getting to that point requires active consistent effort for months or years its a real business that requires real skills and real effort that most people arent willing to put in because they were sold on the idea that it would be easy its not the people making ten thousand dollars or more per month with digital products didnt get there by posting links on reddit and hoping for the best they got there by spending months researching their market until they understood their customers better than the customers understood themselves then creating genuinely valuable products that solve real problems better than existing alternatives building audiences over years by consistently showing up and providing value learning marketing and sales through practice and failure and iteration and treating it like the legitimate business it is rather than a side hustle they can half ass in their spare time what you should actually do starting today if youre serious about making money with digital products and i mean actually serious not ill try this for two weeks and give up when it doesnt work immediately serious then you need to completely change your approach stop posting your product links in seller communities like this one right now just stop it its not working its never going to work and youre wasting time you could spend doing things that actually move the needle instead research where your actual target customers hang out online join those communities and spend time just observing and learning without trying to sell anything start a list of common problems questions and pain points you notice this is your market research foundation over the next few weeks conduct keyword research to understand what your target audience searches for on google start a blog a youtube channel or pinterest account focused on your niche this one works really well pick one platform and commit to it rather than spreading yourself thin across everything create your first few pieces of valuable free content that actually helps people set up an email list with a valuable freebie as a lead magnet that solves a small version of the problem your paid product will solve for the next three months publish content consistently not sporadically when you feel like it but on a schedule two or three pieces per week is realistic for most people or you can use ai for ideas and do it daily engage authentically in communities by helping people and answering questions without mentioning your product build your email list to at least 100 subscribers through your content and lead magnet survey your audience about what they need most what theyre struggling with and what would make their lives easier over the following months create or refine your digital product based on actual audience feedback not your assumptions pre sell to your email list before you even finish the product to validate demand launch with a strategic campaign that builds anticipation collect testimonials from those early customers and iterate based on their feedback to make the product better for the long term scale your content marketing efforts as you learn what works explore paid advertising only after youve validated your offer with organic sales and know your numbers create additional products for your audience once you understand what else they need then build systems and automation so youre not manually doing everything forever do you notice something actual selling doesnt happen until months into this process thats because you cant sell effectively until you understand your market and have built trust with real people who see you as a helpful resource rather than another person trying to take their money stop selling start serving heres the paradigm shift that changes everything stop trying to sell products start trying to solve problems when you focus on genuinely helping your target audience creating free content that actually serves them showing up consistently even when it feels like nobodys paying attention demonstrating expertise through results rather than claims building relationships with individual people who then become advocates selling becomes natural and easy your products become the paid extension of the free value youre already providing people who love your free content and trust your expertise will happily pay for more advanced comprehensive or convenient solutions because theyve already experienced the quality of your work theyre not taking a risk on a stranger theyre investing in someone whos already proven they can help but when you skip straight to selling when you paste your link in communities full of other sellers and hope someone bites youre not solving problems youre making noise and in 2026s saturated market where everyone is competing for attention noise just gets filtered out by our overloaded brains your wakeup call if youre reading this and feeling defensive take a step back and sit with that feeling for a minute im not attacking you personally or saying youre a bad person im attacking the lazy shortcut seeking approach thats been sold to you by people who make their money teaching digital product creation rather than actually selling digital products themselves those gurus have incentives to make it sound easier than it really is because if they told you the truth about how much work it takes you wouldnt buy their course the truth is uncomfortable you got off the bus at the wrong stop the path to success isnt through seller communities where youre competing for scraps of attention its through your customers communities where you become known as the helpful expert its through search engines where people are actively looking for solutions find you its through building trust over time by consistently delivering value the good news now you know you can stop wasting time on strategies that dont work and start investing time in strategies that do you can stop feeling frustrated and
